newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa exports white maize to drought-hit Kenya.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa exports white maize to drought-hit Kenya.

text.p: South African traders have begun exporting white maize to Kenya following a drought which has created food shortages throughout the East African region, industry sources said on Thursday.
At least 70,000 tonnes has already been shipped with more being loaded on to ships. Further quantities from the new harvest, which began last month, is also expected to find its way there, they said.
"We've been exporting white since the beginning of May. About 70,000 (tonnes) has gone out and I would say all of it has gone to Kenya," said a shipping source who asked not to be identified.
Kenyan officials said recently that about 1.5 million people faced food shortages even after the rainy season started.

The country's National Cereals and Produce Board in April tendered for the supply of 80,000 tonnes of white maize in three lots. The first lot had been expected to arrive at Mombasa port in mid May and the other two in June.

Konrad Keyser, director of grain marketing at one of South Africa's biggest agricultural co-operatives, SentraalWes, said that in general white maize would be exported first and in greater quantities this season. Yellow would follow later.
"Exports are in the process of starting up now...I assume the first lots would go up north into Africa," he told Reuters.

South Africa is expected to harvest a commercial crop in 1997 of some 7.660 million tonnes. This would be around two million tonnes below last year's bumper harvest but would leave between one and two million tonnes for export.
The shipping source said several vessels were lined up for further shipments to various parts of the world -- which he did not detail -- and which were expected to carry on until at least September.
Traditional buyers of South African white maize include Japan and the countries of South East Asia.
South African co-operatives said last month that they had been successful in selling 250,000 tonnes of yellow maize to Iran.
